A quieter way to read

By The Gopher team

Reading on the web can be wonderfully useful. It can also be noisy. A consistent text interface lets the words take the lead, with simple links and a predictable way to move between documents. This paragraph is deliberately long enough to help an article extractor distinguish meaningful writing from a navigation menu.

Keep the structure

Headings, paragraphs, code, and lists carry meaning. They should remain in a reading copy. Read the reference guide, jump to this section, or visit a Gopher menu.

A local conversion can read the document that is already loaded, including useful text that a page has added after loading. It does not need an account or a remote processing service. The original page stays available whenever an interactive feature is needed.

  1. Choose a page.
    • Keep meaningful links.
  2. Read without the clutter.
if (quiet) {
  read("text");
}
Good navigation should feel familiar on every page.
